text:
customer-jamie: Hey team — we started seeing truncated streaming responses around 10:23am PST. Client gets a sudden connection close mid-stream and our app logs a 'broken pipe'. Redwood gateway returns a 502 in the SDK. Trace sample: trc_9f4b2a. Affects ~1-2% of streaming calls but spikes under burst load. Can you triage?

support-engr: Sorry you're hitting this, Jamie. Can you paste the SDK version + minimal repro? Also any proxy in front of your app?

customer-jamie: Using redwood-js 0.8.1, Node 18. No customer-side proxy. Minimal repro (Node):
```js
const res = await fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Accept': 'text/event-stream', 'Authorization': 'Bearer ...' },
  body: JSON.stringify({ prompt: 'hi' })
});
res.body.on('data', chunk => console.log(chunk.toString()));
```
We see data for a few seconds then connection closes. No client-side error before close.

ops-bot: Trace trc_9f4b2a created: upstream connection FIN observed prior to final chunk trailer. Proxy: gw-prod-12.

alex: Thanks — that pattern (upstream FIN before chunk trailer) usually means the gateway or one of our front proxies shredded the TCP connection while the runtime was still streaming. Two hypotheses: 1) client half-close racing with proxy idle/read timeouts, or 2) intermediary (nginx/edge) hitting an upstream_read_timeout during slow token production.

maya: I pulled the trace. There are ~120ms stalls between chunk writes in some requests (model slowdown). Gateway has default upstream_read_timeout=30s, but we see a lot of per-connection short pauses that coincide with FINs. Also metrics show an increase in "upstream_fd_closed_by_proxy" counters for gw-prod-12.

support-engr: Jamie — quick mitigation to try on your side: enable keepalive pings from your client or send a small whitespace every 4s while consuming. That prevents some intermediaries from deciding the client vanished.

customer-jamie: Ok trying a quick patch to send a 1-byte comment every 3s. Will report back.

emma: We should also avoid counting these as 5xx in billing/alerts. Opening internal ticket INC-1234 to track: "gateway-classify-client-disconnect-as-5xx". Assigning to eng-sre.

alex: Action items from runtime side: (a) confirm gateway treats client-originated FIN specially (b) add a better diagnostic tag in traces when proxy sends FIN upstream, (c) short-term: increase upstream_read_timeout on gw-prod-12 to 60s for streaming routes while we investigate.

maya: I pushed a canary change to gw-prod-12 config (streaming route) to extend read timeout in canary pool. Watching error rate. If it drops we can roll.

ops-bot: Deploy canary started: canary-id cny_20240324_gw12.

support-engr: For engineering repro, you can simulate the pause with curl:
```bash
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer ..." -d @payload.json https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream --no-buffer
# then manually pause the server or insert delays to reproduce FIN-before-trailer
```
Also a netcat-based repro: send chunked frames and then send FIN before sending terminating 0 chunk.

alex: Long-term fix candidates: treat client-initiated resets as non-5xx in metering, improve gateway logic to wait a bit longer on upstream slowdowns when model is producing occasional tokens, and expose an SDK toggle for automatic keepalive pings.

customer-jamie: Patch applied: sending a tiny "\n" every 3s. After 2h load test the failures dropped from 1.8% to 0.12%. Looks promising. :thumbsup:

emma: Noted — INC-1234 created and linked to runtime playbook. We'll follow up with a postmortem if canary shows a rollout candidate.

support-engr: Jamie — can you DM the sample trace IDs and request IDs if you see any more? We'll keep monitoring.

customer-jamie: Will do, thanks everyone.

alex: Keeping this open until canary stabilizes. If the gateway change doesn't fully resolve, next step is an engineered change to how we classify/label client resets in the billing/alerts pipeline.

maya: Current status: canary reduced proxy-FIN incidents by ~85% over a 3h window. Leaving canary running and preparing a staggered roll.

support-engr: Closing loop for customer: recommended workaround (keepalive bytes) + we rolled canary to reduce proxy premature closes. Follow-up: internal ticket for metering classification.

customer-jamie: Thanks, appreciate the fast turnaround.
